mechanism_narrative: A surge in housing starts (HOUST) above 1800K units, indicating robust demand, boosts consumer discretionary spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical correlation between HOUST and consumer spending
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 50% of instances when HOUST surpasses 1800K, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.5% signals an accommodative monetary environment, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as investors seek higher yields.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) drops below 3.5% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) grows by more than 200K in a month, the tightening labor market drives wage inflation, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical relationship between labor market and inflation
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 6-month moving average signals strengthening supply chains, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as manufacturers' profitability improves.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) when INDPRO surpasses its 6-month MA.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the GDP annual growth rate (GDPC1) below 2% indicates slowing demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, as investors reassess growth prospects.
evidence_refs: fact:historical relationship between GDP growth and equity markets
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 55% of triggered instances, or Rank IC < 0.015 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The difference between FEDFUNDS and the 10-year Treasury yield (proxied by RSAFS growth) widening beyond 150bps signals a flattening yield curve, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as investors anticipate economic slowdown.
evidence_refs: fact:historical relationship between yield curve and economic activity
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 50% of triggered instances, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Always-on: the lower the unemployment rate (UNRATE), the higher the pressure on wages, potentially leading to higher inflation and, consequently, negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.01 over any 3-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) at low UNRATE levels.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) growth exceeds 3% YoY and housing starts (HOUST) are above 1600K, the combination of inflation and robust demand drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days, as investors bet on sustained economic growth.
evidence_refs: fact:historical relationship between inflation, demand, and equity markets
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 45% of triggered instances, or Rank IC < 0.025 over any 2-year rolling window.
